### Observed differences

- The order between the A32/A33 pair and the A26/A28 pair is reversed. Before, A32 came before A26 in about 99 in 100 traces and before A28 in essentially all traces (A33 similarly, about 98–99 in 100); in the later window, A26 comes before A32/A33 in about 97 in 100 traces and A28 before A32/A33 in about 97–98 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- Direct successors changed accordingly. Before, A25 was followed next by A32 (about 55 in 100) or A33 (about 45 in 100); in the later window A25 is followed next by A26 in about 96 in 100. Before, A28 was followed by A29 in about 98 in 100; in the later window it is followed by A32 or A33 (about 49 in 100 each). A32 and A33, which previously led mainly to A26 or to each other, now lead to A29 in about 47–49 in 100 of their outgoing transitions. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Event distances moved in the same direction: A26 now follows A25 after about 1 step (96 in 100) instead of about 3; A28 follows A25 after about 3 steps instead of 5; A32 and A33 now follow A25 only after about 4–5 steps (previously 1–2); A29 now follows A32/A33 after 1–2 steps (previously 4–5) and follows A28 after about 3 steps (previously 1). [LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- Participation of these activities did not change — A26, A28, A32 and A33 still appear in every trace — but their relative positions shifted: A26 (mean position about 0.49 to 0.44) and A28 (about 0.57 to 0.50) occur earlier, A32 and A33 (about 0.45 to 0.55 each) later. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- A secondary, weakly supported difference: A02 appears in fewer traces (about 23 in 100 before vs about 14 in 100 after) and its outgoing transitions are much less concentrated on A15 (about 89% vs 38%, based on only 46 vs 26 traces); A14 also leads to A02 less often (about 20% vs 5% of its outgoing transitions) and to A15 more often (about 79% vs 90%). [POS001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment formed by A32 and A33 (which typically follow one another) is placed differently: in the later window the flow reads A25 → A26 → A28 → A32/A33 → A29, whereas in the earlier window it read A25 → A32/A33 → A26 → A28 → A29. This rests on direct relational evidence — the pairwise order of A32/A33 versus A26/A28 is reversed in about 97–99 in 100 traces — and is consistent across the successor changes, event distances and relative positions, observed on essentially all 200 traces in each window, with unchanged participation for all activities involved. The number of flagged items (22, against roughly 0.62 expected if nothing had changed) also cannot be explained by chance screening as a whole. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG009, LAG010, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: with only two aggregate windows, the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering applied within traces from a shift in the mix of two process variants in which both orders already existed at different frequencies. The A02/A14 differences rest on few observations (roughly 14–46 traces) and may reflect rare-variant sampling rather than change; they are not needed for the reordering hypothesis. Positions are event positions, so "earlier/later" refers to sequence placement, not clock time. [POS001, DIR001, LAG001, LAG002]
